senses.definition: used before countable or singular nouns referring to people or things that have not already been mentioned

examples.x: a man/horse/unit
an aunt/egg/hour/X-ray
I can only carry two at a time.
There's a visitor for you.
She's a friend of my father's (= one of my father's friends).

senses.definition: used to show that somebody/something is a member of a group or profession

examples.x: Their new car's a BMW.
She's a Buddhist.
He's a teacher.
Is that a Monet (= a painting by Monet)?

senses.definition: any; every

examples.x: A lion is a dangerous animal.

senses.definition: used before uncountable nouns when these have an adjective in front of them, or phrase following them

examples.x: a good knowledge of French
a sadness that won’t go away

senses.definition: used in front of two nouns that are seen as a single unit

examples.x: a knife and fork

senses.definition: used instead of one before some numbers

examples.x: A thousand people were there.

senses.definition: used when talking about prices, quantities and rates

examples.x: They cost 50p a kilo.
I can type 50 words a minute.
He was driving at 50 miles an hour.

senses.definition: a person like somebody

examples.x: She's a little Greta Thunberg.

senses.definition: used before somebody’s name to show that the speaker does not know the person

examples.x: There's a Mrs Green to see you.

senses.definition: used before the names of days of the week to talk about one particular day

examples.x: She died on a Tuesday.

senses.definition: a little more or less than; a little before or after

examples.x: It costs about $10.
They waited (for) about an hour.
He arrived (at) about ten.

senses.definition: nearly; very close to

examples.x: I'm just about ready.
This is about the best we can hope for.

senses.definition: in many directions; here and there

examples.x: The children were rushing about in the garden.

senses.definition: in no particular order; in various places

examples.x: Her books were lying about on the floor.

senses.definition: doing nothing in particular

examples.x: People were standing about in the road.

senses.definition: able to be found in a place

examples.x: There was nobody about.
There's a lot of flu about.
She’s somewhere about—I saw her a few minutes ago.

senses.definition: facing the opposite direction

examples.x: He brought the ship about.

senses.definition: almost; very nearly

examples.x: I've met just about everyone.
‘Did you reach your sales target?’ ‘Just about.’

senses.definition: approximately

examples.x: She should be arriving just about now.

senses.definition: able to go outside again after an illness
travelling around a place

examples.x: We've been out and about talking to people all over the country.

senses.definition: used to say that you have finished telling somebody about something and there is nothing to add

examples.x: ‘Anything else?’ ‘No, that's about it for now.’

senses.definition: at or to a higher place

examples.x: Put it on the shelf above.
Seen from above the cars looked tiny.
I could hear somebody calling out my name from up above.
They were acting on instructions from above (= from somebody in a higher position of authority).

senses.definition: greater in number, level or age

examples.x: increases of 5% and above
A score of 70 or above will get you an ‘A’.
children aged 12 and above

senses.definition: earlier in something written or printed

examples.x: As was stated above…
See above, page 97.
My client is the mother of the two above-named children.

senses.definition: (to do) even more than is expected or demanded

examples.x: Our staff members will go above and beyond to ensure that our customers are satisfied.

senses.definition: as stated or reported by somebody/something

examples.x: According to Mick, it's a great movie.
You've been absent six times according to our records.

senses.definition: following, agreeing with or depending on something

examples.x: The work was done according to her instructions.
Everything went according to plan.
The salary will be fixed according to qualifications and experience.

senses.definition: to do only what you have enough money to do and no more

examples.x: We wanted to buy a bigger house than this but it was a case of cutting our coat according to our cloth.

senses.definition: in a way that is appropriate to what has been done or said in a particular situation

examples.x: We have to discover his plans and act accordingly.

senses.definition: for that reason

examples.x: The cost of materials rose sharply last year. Accordingly, we were forced to increase our prices.

senses.definition: from one side to the other side

examples.x: It's too wide. We can't swim across.
The yard measures about 50 feet across.

senses.definition: in a particular direction towards or at somebody/something

examples.x: When my name was called, he looked across at me.

senses.definition: opposite

examples.x: There's a school just across from our house.

senses.definition: written from side to side

examples.x: I can't do 3 across.

senses.definition: used in speaking to emphasize a fact or a comment, or that something is really true

examples.x: What did she actually say?
It's not actually raining now.
The book was never actually published.
I'm glad we were actually able to get the message across.
That's the only reason I'm actually going.
There are lots of people there who can actually help you.
I didn't want to say anything without actually reading the letter first.

senses.definition: used to show a contrast between what is true and what somebody believes, and to show surprise about this contrast

examples.x: It was actually kind of fun after all.
The food was not actually all that expensive.
Our turnover actually increased last year.
I couldn't believe it had all actually happened.

senses.definition: used to correct somebody in a polite way

examples.x: We're not American, actually. We're Canadian.
Actually, it would be much more sensible to do it later.
They're not married, actually.

senses.definition: used to get somebody’s attention, to introduce a new topic or to say something that somebody may not like, in a polite way

examples.x: Actually, I'll be a bit late home.
Actually, I'm busy at the moment—can I call you back?
Well, actually, I think she's done a pretty good job.

senses.definition: later in time; afterwards

examples.x: That was in 1996. Soon after, I heard that he'd died.
I could come next week, or the week after.
And they all lived happily ever after.

senses.definition: at a later time; after an event that has already been mentioned

examples.x: Afterwards she was sorry for what she'd said.
Let's go out now and eat afterwards.
Shortly afterwards he met her again.
He went to dinner at a restaurant, and soon afterwards, he fell ill.

senses.definition: one more time; on another occasion

examples.x: This must never happen again.
Try again—it takes practice.
Can we start again, please?
Could you say it again, please?
When will I see you again?
This author again proves to be a superb storyteller.
I've told you again and again (= many times) not to do that.
I'll have to write it all over again (= again from the beginning).
She tried over and over again (= many times) to get it right.
He has yet again (= as has happened many times before) shown that he cannot be trusted.
Once again (= as had happened several times before), the train was late.

senses.definition: showing that somebody/something is in the same place or state that they were in originally

examples.x: We're very happy to be here together again.
He was glad to be home again.
You'll soon feel well again.
She spends two hours a day getting to work and back again.

senses.definition: added to an amount that is already there

examples.x: The cost is about half as much again as it was two years ago.
I'd like the same again (= the same amount or the same thing).

senses.definition: used to show that a comment or fact is connected with what you have just said

examples.x: And again, we must think of the cost.

senses.definition: used to introduce a fact or an opinion that contrasts with what you have just said

examples.x: We might buy it but then again we might not.

senses.definition: used when you ask somebody to tell you something or repeat something that you think they have told you already

examples.x: What was the name again?

senses.definition: from time to time; occasionally

examples.x: Every now and again she checked to see if he was still asleep.

senses.definition: used to ask somebody to serve you the same drink as before

examples.x: Same again, please!

senses.definition: often; on many or all occasions

examples.x: You will get a perfect result time after time if you follow these instructions.
Time and again, the girls have shown how strong and determined they can be.

senses.definition: opposing or disagreeing with somebody/something

examples.x: the fight against terrorism
We're playing against the league champions next week.
We were rowing against the current.
That's against the law.
Employees can't be forced to join a union against their will.
Are you for or against the death penalty?
She is against seeing (= does not want to see) him.
I'd advise you against doing that.

senses.definition: not to the advantage or favour of somebody/something

examples.x: The evidence is against him.
Her age is against her.

senses.definition: close to, touching or hitting somebody/something

examples.x: Put the piano there, against the wall.
The rain beat against the windows.

senses.definition: in order to prevent something from happening or to reduce the damage caused by something

examples.x: an injection against rabies
They took precautions against fire.
Are we insured against theft?
He gritted his teeth against the pain.

senses.definition: with something in the background, as a contrast

examples.x: His red clothes stood out clearly against the snow.
The love story unfolds against a background of civil war.

senses.definition: used when you are comparing two things

examples.x: You must weigh the benefits against the cost.
Check your receipts against the statement.
What's the rate of exchange against the dollar?

senses.definition: if you include money or costs against an amount that is owed, you use it to reduce the amount

examples.x: The accountant said I could offset all my travel costs against tax.

senses.definition: if you borrow money against property that you own, you use the value of the property as a guarantee that you will repay the money

examples.x: They had borrowed a lot of money against the value of the house.

senses.definition: in contrast with something

examples.x: They got 27 per cent of the vote as against 32 per cent at the last election.

senses.definition: you are unlikely to succeed because the conditions are not good for you
used in expressions of time with the simple past tense to show how far in the past something happened

examples.x: two weeks/months/years ago
The letter came a few days ago.
She was here just a minute ago.
a short/long time ago
How long ago did you buy it?
It was on TV not (so) long ago.
Scientists think there was water on Mars a long time ago.
He stopped working some time ago (= quite a long time ago).
They're getting married? It's not that long ago (= it's only a short time ago) that they met!

senses.definition: further forward in space or time; in front

examples.x: I'll run ahead and warn them.
The road ahead was blocked.
We've got a lot of hard work ahead.
This will create problems in the months ahead.
He was looking straight ahead (= straight forward, in front of him).

senses.definition: earlier

examples.x: The party was planned weeks ahead.

senses.definition: winning; further advanced

examples.x: Our team was ahead by six points.
You need to work hard to keep ahead.

senses.definition: although

examples.x: He finally agreed, albeit reluctantly, to help us.

senses.definition: very similar

examples.x: My sister and I do not look alike.
Airports are all alike to me.
Though John and Andrew look exactly alike, they act quite differently.

senses.definition: completely

examples.x: She was dressed all in white.
He lives all alone.
The coffee went all over my skirt.

senses.definition: very

examples.x: She was all excited.
Now don't get all upset about it.

senses.definition: used to show that something is more than you would like

examples.x: I'm all too aware of the problems.
The end of the trip came all too soon.

senses.definition: to each side

examples.x: The score was four all.

senses.definition: all the time; from the beginning

examples.x: I realized it was in my pocket all along.

senses.definition: in every way; in all respects

examples.x: a good performance all around

senses.definition: for each person

examples.x: She bought drinks all around.

senses.definition: so much better, harder, etc.

examples.x: We'll have to work all the harder with two people off sick.
Her difficult childhood makes her achievements all the more remarkable.

senses.definition: almost

examples.x: The party was all but over when we arrived.
It was all but impossible to read his writing.

senses.definition: everything or everyone except something/somebody

examples.x: All but one of the plates were damaged.

senses.definition: physically tired

examples.x: At the end of the race he felt all in.

senses.definition: including everything

examples.x: The trip cost £750 all in.

senses.definition: used to emphasize an amount, a size, etc. usually when it is very small

examples.x: It must be all of 100 metres to the car!

senses.definition: everywhere

examples.x: We looked all over for the ring.

senses.definition: what you would expect of the person mentioned

examples.x: That sounds like my sister all over.

senses.definition: in every way; in all respects

examples.x: a good performance all round

senses.definition: for each person

examples.x: She bought drinks all round.

senses.definition: (not) having a healthy mind; (not) thinking clearly

examples.x: My dog behaves very oddly at times—I don't think he's quite all there.

senses.definition: used to say what the most important aspect of something is

examples.x: It's all about money these days.

senses.definition: to believe strongly that something should be done

examples.x: They're all for saving money where they can.

senses.definition: to show a lot of interest in or enthusiasm for somebody

examples.x: He was all over her at the party.

senses.definition: to be very attractive or impressive

examples.x: He thinks he's all that.

senses.definition: to be the end for somebody

examples.x: It looks as though it's all up with us now (= we are ruined, have no further chances, etc.).

senses.definition: acceptable; in an acceptable manner

examples.x: Is the coffee all right?
Are you getting along all right in your new job?
‘They're off to Spain next week.’ ‘It's all right for some, isn't it?’ (= some people are lucky)
‘How was your trip?’ ‘All right.’

senses.definition: safe and well

examples.x: I hope the children are all right.
Do you feel all right?

senses.definition: only just good enough

examples.x: Your work is all right but I'm sure you could do better.

senses.definition: that can be allowed

examples.x: Are you sure it's all right for me to leave early?

senses.definition: used to emphasize that there is no doubt about something

examples.x: ‘Are you sure it's her?’ ‘Oh, it's her all right.’

senses.definition: a person that you think is sexually attractive
used by or about somebody who is happy with their own life and does not care about other people’s problems
used to say that a performance, an event, etc. will be successful even if the preparations for it have not gone well
used to refuse an offer or invitation, especially one that you think is unreasonable or not very good

examples.x: ‘Could I interest you in our special offer?’ ‘No, you're all right, mate.’

senses.definition: not quite

examples.x: I like almost all of them.
They'll eat almost anything.
Almost no one (= hardly anyone) believed him.
The castle is almost entirely surrounded by water.
It's a mistake they almost always make.
The painting is almost certainly a forgery.
Her handwriting is almost impossible to read.
The team faces almost certain defeat in today's match.
The workforce has almost doubled in the past ten years.
I almost forgot your birthday.
Housing has become almost as big a problem as education.
The story seems almost too strange to be true.

senses.definition: without any other people

examples.x: Tom is not alone in finding Rick hard to work with.
She waited until she was alone with him to speak.
He was afraid of being alone with his thoughts.
He lives alone.
She was sitting all alone in the hall.
Finally the two of us were alone together.
I don't like going out alone at night.

senses.definition: without the help of other people or things

examples.x: It's hard bringing up children alone.
The assassin said he had acted alone.

senses.definition: lonely and unhappy or without any friends

examples.x: Carol felt all alone in the world.
I've been so alone since you went away.

senses.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to show that the person or thing mentioned is the only one

examples.x: You can't blame anyone else; you alone made the decision.

senses.definition: used after a noun or pronoun to emphasize one particular thing

examples.x: The shoes alone cost £200.

senses.definition: to do something without help from anyone

examples.x: Andrew decided to go it alone and start his own business.

senses.definition: to stop annoying somebody or trying to get their attention

examples.x: She's asked to be left alone but the press photographers follow her everywhere.
Don't touch me! Leave me alone!

senses.definition: to stop touching, changing, or moving something

examples.x: I've told you before—leave my things alone!

senses.definition: used after a statement to emphasize that because the first thing is not true or possible, the next thing cannot be true or possible either

examples.x: There isn't enough room for us, let alone any guests.
I didn’t have any clothes, let alone a passport.

senses.definition: to be independent or not connected with other people, organizations or ideas

examples.x: These islands are too small to stand alone as independent states.
The problems that research is designed to solve do not stand alone, but are part of a wider context.

senses.definition: to be not near other objects or buildings

examples.x: The arch once stood alone at the entrance to the castle.

senses.definition: used to say that you will have to wait for some time to find out the result of a situation

examples.x: Only time will tell if the treatment has been successful.

senses.definition: forward

examples.x: I was just walking along singing to myself.
He pointed out various landmarks as we drove along.

senses.definition: with somebody

examples.x: We're going for a swim. Why don't you come along?
I'll be along (= I'll join you) in a few minutes.

senses.definition: towards a better state or position

examples.x: The book's coming along nicely.

senses.definition: in addition to somebody/something; in the same way as somebody/something

examples.x: She lost her job when the factory closed, along with hundreds of others.

senses.definition: next to or at the side of something

examples.x: A police car pulled up alongside us.
a lifeboat moored alongside the yacht
Much of the land alongside the river is below sea level.

senses.definition: together with or at the same time as something/somebody

examples.x: Traditional beliefs still flourish alongside a modern urban lifestyle.

senses.definition: before now or before a particular time in the past

examples.x: ‘Lunch?’ ‘No thanks, I've already eaten.’
We got there early but Mike had already left.
By 2025, filming of the sequel was already under way.
Much of what he said I knew already.

senses.definition: used to express surprise that something has happened so soon or so early

examples.x: Is it 10 o'clock already?
You're not leaving already, are you?

senses.definition: used to emphasize that a situation or problem exists

examples.x: I'm already late.
The new company already has an excellent reputation.
There are far too many people already. We can't take any more.

senses.definition: used after a word or phrase to show that you are annoyed

examples.x: Just stop already, no one feels sorry for you.

senses.definition: used to say that something is annoying or boring and that you want it to stop
in addition; too

examples.x: She's fluent in French and German. She also speaks a little Italian.
rubella, also known as German measles
I didn't like it that much. Also, it was much too expensive.
Jake's father had also been a doctor (= both Jake and his father were doctors).
She was not only intelligent but also very musical.
He also recently said that he would be leaving at the end of the year.
I probably also have a copy of the list.

senses.definition: used for introducing a statement that makes the main statement in a sentence seem surprising

examples.x: Although the sun was shining, it wasn't very warm.
Although small, the kitchen is well designed.

senses.definition: used to mean ‘but’ or ‘however’ when you are commenting on a statement

examples.x: I felt he was wrong, although I didn't say so at the time.

senses.definition: (used to emphasize something) completely; in every way

examples.x: The train went slower and slower until it stopped altogether.
I don't altogether agree with you.
I am not altogether happy (= I am very unhappy) about the decision.
It was an altogether different situation.
I’m not altogether convinced, I’m afraid.

senses.definition: used to give a total number or amount

examples.x: You owe me £68 altogether.

senses.definition: used to introduce a summary when you have mentioned a number of different things

examples.x: The food was good and we loved the music. Altogether it was a great evening.

senses.definition: at all times; on every occasion

examples.x: There's almost always somebody at home in the evenings.
Always lock your car.
She always arrives at 7.30.
The children always seem to be hungry.
Success seems always to be out of reach.
Your ideas are always welcome.
It's not always easy to do the right thing.
We're not always this busy!

senses.definition: for a long time; since you can remember

examples.x: Pat has always loved gardening.
This is the way we've always done it.
This painting is very good—Ellie always was very good at art (= so it is not very surprising).
Did you always want to be an actor?

senses.definition: for all future time

examples.x: I'll always love you.

senses.definition: if you say a person is always doing something, or something is always happening, you mean that they do it, or it happens, very often, and that this is annoying

examples.x: She's always criticizing me.
That phone's always ringing.
Why are you always complaining about my cooking?

senses.definition: used to suggest a possible course of action

examples.x: If it doesn't fit, you can always take it back.
If he can't help, there's always John.

senses.definition: as usually happens or is expected

examples.x: As always, Polly was late for school.

senses.definition: used to say that somebody cannot change

examples.x: Once an actor, always an actor.

senses.definition: in the middle of or during something, especially something that causes excitement or fear

examples.x: He finished his speech amid tremendous applause.
The firm collapsed amid allegations of fraud.

senses.definition: surrounded by something

examples.x: The hotel was in a beautiful position amid lemon groves.

senses.definition: surrounded by somebody/something; in the middle of somebody/something

examples.x: a house among the trees
They strolled among the crowds.
I found the letter amongst his papers.
It's OK, you're among friends now.

senses.definition: being included or happening in groups of things or people

examples.x: A British woman was among the survivors.
He was among the last to leave.
This attitude is common among the under-25s.
‘What was wrong with the job?’ ‘Well, the pay wasn't good, among other things.’
Discuss it among yourselves (= with each other) first.

senses.definition: used when you are dividing or choosing something, and three or more people or things are involved

examples.x: They divided the money up among their three children.

senses.definition: also; in addition to

examples.x: bread and butter
a table, two chairs and a desk
Sue and I left early.
Do it slowly and carefully.
Can he read and write?
I cooked lunch. And I made a cake. (= you are emphasizing how much you have done)

senses.definition: then; following this

examples.x: She came in and took her coat off.

senses.definition: used before a verb instead of to, to show purpose

examples.x: Go and get me a pen please.
I'll come and see you soon.
We stopped and bought some bread.

senses.definition: used to introduce a comment or a question

examples.x: ‘We talked for hours.’ ‘And what did you decide?’

senses.definition: as a result

examples.x: Miss another class and you'll fail.

senses.definition: added to

examples.x: 5 and 5 makes 10.
What's 47 and 16?

senses.definition: used between repeated words to show that something is repeated or continuing

examples.x: He tried and tried but without success.
The pain got worse and worse.

senses.definition: used between repeated words to show that there are important differences between things or people of the same kind

examples.x: I like city life but there are cities and cities.

senses.definition: one more; an extra thing or person

examples.x: Would you like another drink?
‘Finished?’ ‘No, I've got another three questions to do.’
We've still got another (= a further) forty miles to go.
‘It's a bill.’ ‘Oh no, not another!’
I got another of those calls yesterday.

senses.definition: different; a different person or thing

examples.x: Let's do it another time.
We can try that—but whether it'll work is another matter.
The room's too small. Let's see if they've got another one.
I don't like this room. I'm going to ask for another.

senses.definition: a person or thing of a very similar type

examples.x: Maybe she's going to be another Taylor Swift (= as famous as her).
There'll never be another like him.

senses.definition: used when you are referring to various types of a thing, without saying exactly what you mean

examples.x: We've all got problems of one kind or another.

senses.definition: first one person or thing, and then another, and then another, up to any number or amount

examples.x: The bills kept coming in, one after another.

senses.definition: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb in negative sentences or questions, meaning ‘at all’

examples.x: He wasn't any good at French.
I can't run any faster.
Is your father feeling any better?
I don't want any more.
If you don't tell them, nobody will be any the wiser (= they will not find out about it).

senses.definition: used at the end of a negative sentence to mean ‘at all’

examples.x: That won't hurt you any.

senses.definition: often used at the end of negative sentences and at the end of questions, to mean ‘any longer’

examples.x: She doesn't live here any more.
Why doesn't he speak to me any more?
Now she won't have to go out to work any more.

senses.definition: used instead of somebody in negative sentences and in questions after if/whether, and after verbs such as prevent, forbid, avoid, etc.

examples.x: Is there anybody who can help me?
Anybody can use the pool—you don't need to be a member.
She wasn't anybody before she got that job.

senses.definition: any person at all; it does not matter who
an important person
used instead of someone in negative sentences and in questions after if/whether, and after verbs such as prevent, forbid, avoid, etc.

examples.x: Is anyone there?
Does anyone else want to come?
Did anyone see you?
Hardly anyone came.
I forbid anyone to touch that clock.

senses.definition: any person at all; it does not matter who

examples.x: Anybody can see that it's wrong.
The exercises are so simple that almost anyone can do them.

senses.definition: an important person

examples.x: She wasn't anyone before she got that job.

senses.definition: used instead of something in negative sentences and in questions; after if/whether; and after verbs such as prevent, ban, avoid, etc.

examples.x: Would you like anything else?
There's never anything worth watching on TV.
If you remember anything at all, please let us know.
We hope to prevent anything unpleasant from happening.

senses.definition: any thing at all, when it does not matter which

examples.x: I'm so hungry, I'll eat anything.

senses.definition: any thing of importance

examples.x: Is there anything (= any truth) in these rumours?

senses.definition: definitely not

examples.x: The hotel was anything but cheap.
It wasn't cheap. Anything but.

senses.definition: similar to somebody/something

examples.x: He isn't anything like my first boss.

senses.definition: very happy, quick, etc.

examples.x: I felt as pleased as anything.

senses.definition: very much

examples.x: They're always slagging me off like anything.

senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is not as good, not enough, etc.

examples.x: The book wasn't anything like as good as her first one.

senses.definition: definitely not

examples.x: I wouldn't give it up for anything.

senses.definition: or another thing of a similar type

examples.x: If you want to call a meeting or anything, just let me know.

senses.definition: used when adding something to support an idea or argument

examples.x: It's too expensive and anyway the colour doesn't suit you.
We're not perfect, but it doesn't really matter anyway.
It's too late now, anyway.

senses.definition: despite something; even so

examples.x: It's going to happen anyway, so we won't object to it.
I'm afraid we can't come, but thanks for the invitation anyway.
She told them what would happen and they went ahead anyway.
Development money often goes to companies that would have come here anyway.
The water was cold but I took a shower anyway.

senses.definition: used when changing the subject of a conversation, ending the conversation or returning to a subject

examples.x: So, anyway, back to what I was saying.
Anyway, I'd better go now—I'll see you tomorrow.
Anyway, let's forget about that for the moment.

senses.definition: used to correct or slightly change what you have said

examples.x: I think she's right. I hope so, anyway.
She works in a bank. She did when I last saw her, anyway.

senses.definition: used in negative sentences and in questions instead of somewhere

It's sure to rain.
You’re sure to get lost if you don’t keep to the path.

senses.definition: that can be trusted or relied on

examples.x: It's a sure sign of economic recovery.

senses.definition: steady and confident

examples.x: We admired her sure touch at the keyboard.

senses.definition: used to tell somebody to do something

examples.x: Be sure to give your family my regards.

senses.definition: without doubt

examples.x: No one knows for sure what happened.

examples.x: He's a good bet to earn a spot on the US team.

senses.definition: very confident

examples.x: She seems very sure of herself.

senses.definition: used to say ‘yes’ to a suggestion or request

examples.x: ‘Are you coming?’ ‘Sure thing.’

senses.definition: used to admit that something is true

examples.x: He is intelligent, to be sure, but he's also very lazy.

senses.definition: used to show that you are almost certain of what you are saying and want other people to agree with you

examples.x: Surely we should do something about it?

senses.definition: without doubt; certainly

senses.definition: used to say ‘yes’ to somebody or to agree to something

senses.definition: the outside or top layer of something
